summary: Backend e2e tested for Zoom Services clone. 26/27 pytest tests passed (1 skipped automatically because admin's usage was far from limit; usage-limit enforcement was then validated separately via direct DB seeding -> returned HTTP 400 'Usage limit exceeded (14998/15000)'). Auth (cookies + Bearer), brute-force-aware login, task lifecycle (immediate active, scheduled->active transition, active->completed via poller), cancel/delete/bulk-delete, download, name-files full CRUD with duplicate + whitespace handling, builtin Indian/English pools, stats, and security (401 on all protected endpoints) all working.

minor.issue: allow_origins='*' combined with allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec; browsers will reject credentialed cross-origin requests. Same-origin (preview URL) works because no CORS preflight needed, but if used cross-origin, cookies would not be sent. Recommend setting explicit origin list in CORS_ORIGINS when used cross-origin.

Lockout logic only triggers when an attempt record already exists (lock truthy) AND count+1>=5, so the 5th attempt is what locks. Works, but `locked_until` is reset to None on failures 1-4 even if previously set in the same window — minor edge. Also lockout is per (IP+email) — testing with random emails won't lock the admin account, which is good.
secure=False on cookies. OK for HTTP testing but for production over HTTPS, secure=True is recommended (browser still accepts secure cookies on HTTPS).

Usage is incremented at task creation time, not on actual completion. If a task is cancelled or fails, the usage counter is not decremented. This matches the 'Usage: x / 15000' UI pattern described, so likely intentional, but worth confirming with product owner.

action_items: Consider tightening CORS_ORIGINS for production deployment (replace '*' with explicit origin list when credentials are enabled).
Consider setting cookie secure=True when serving over HTTPS in production.
Decide whether to decrement user.usage when a task is cancelled (currently does not).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py (~580 lines) is single-file — acceptable for MVP but should be split into routers (auth/tasks/name-files/stats) + db module + auth utils as it grows.
CORS allow_origins='*' + allow_credentials=True is misconfigured per CORS spec; replace '*' with explicit origin list (env-driven) before going cross-origin.
Usage counter is incremented on task creation but never decremented on cancel/fail; confirm product intent.
All routes use Pydantic input validation, exclude _id, return proper status codes, and use async motor — good.
task_poller cycle is 5s — short sleeps for scheduled->active and active->completed transitions (8-16s) work reliably.
